findings.evidence:
`pkg/executor/brie.go:552` compares `e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().SQLKiller.HandleSignal() == exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`.
But `pkg/util/sqlkiller/sqlkiller.go:51-55` returns `exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted.GenWithStackByArgs()` / `exeerrors.ErrMaxExecTimeExceeded.GenWithStackByArgs()`, which (via pingcap/errors) wraps the base error with stack, so `== exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted` will never match.
findings.fix:
Change the BRIE kill monitor to not use `==` on errors. Minimal behavioral-preserving fix:
- `err := e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().SQLKiller.HandleSignal(); if exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted.Equal(err) { ... }`
Safer fix (also cancels on max-exec-time / OOM signals):
- `if err := ...HandleSignal(); err != nil { bq.cancelTask(taskID); return }`
findings.impact: `KILL QUERY` will not be observed by the BRIE executor’s polling goroutine, so long-running `BACKUP`/`RESTORE` via BRIE may not be cancelable promptly (or at all) through kill, potentially leaving heavy background work running and violating expected session/query cancellation semantics.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on later history: `upstream/master:pkg/executor/brie.go:606` still uses `SQLKiller.HandleSignal() == exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`.
findings.verify: Manual repro: start a long-running BRIE `BACKUP`/`RESTORE` statement; from another session run `KILL QUERY <conn_id>`; expect BRIE statement to exit quickly and the BR task to stop (progress halts, no further work/logs). Add a regression test that asserts kill triggers `bq.cancelTask` for BRIE.
findings.what: BRIE kill monitoring uses `==` to compare the error returned by `SQLKiller.HandleSignal()` against `exeerrors.ErrQueryInterrupted`, but `HandleSignal()` returns a stack-wrapped error, so the comparison is always false and BRIE tasks won’t be canceled on kill.

subject: *: unified the cancel/kill logic in tidb (#47063)
summary: This commit replaces `SessionVars.Killed` with `SessionVars.SQLKiller` and updates multiple executor/expression/statistics loops to use `SQLKiller.HandleSignal()` plus typed OOM/max-time errors. A High-severity bug remains in `pkg/executor/brie.go` where kill detection compares errors using `==`, which will never match stack-wrapped errors returned by `HandleSignal()`.
